sources.entry: W - Lightweight, mutli-user, flat-file-database Wiki engine. Create pages quickly and edit them in your Web browser using Mardown/HTML/CSS/JS. The main difference with other wiki is that you are encouraged to customize each page style individually. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: W-CMS is a lightweight, multi-user, flat-file CMS and wiki where pages are created quickly and edited in the browser using Markdown, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with per-page styling.
summary.what_it_does: W is a lightweight CMS aimed at artists and experimental projects, letting users create pages quickly and edit them in a web browser. Pages can be written in Markdown, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and each page can be styled individually. It includes a media manager, multi-user support, and a flat-file database so no database server is needed. Pages can be public or private and linked to each other, and a graph view of links is shown. The README also lists an experimental API (v0), geolocation maps from page coordinates (beta), LDAP authentication (beta), and image optimization on upload. It also says it works without JavaScript.
use_cases: build an experimental or artistic website
quick note-taking that turns into web pages
interactive fiction or branching text games
mind-map style linked pages with private and public sections
how_to_run: Install on a server with Apache (nginx also possible) and PHP >=7.4.0 with curl, mbstring, xml and intl extensions
Download the latest release zip from GitHub and unzip it in the hosted folder, then open it in a browser and follow the setup steps
Or install from sources: clone the git repository
Run make vendor (PHP dependencies), then optionally make build (JS dependencies)
For development, run make serve for a dev server, and make watch for webpack in watch mode
To update from git: git pull, git checkout TAG, make build
notable: Flat-file database with no SQL server needed
Per-page custom CSS and JavaScript, not just a shared theme
Pages double as notes, websites and private drafts, with links between them
Works with editing via URL suffix such as ../edit
Optional image optimization for uploads using gd or imagick
caveats: Geolocation and LDAP authentication are marked BETA
The API is described as experimental (v0)
Server requirements are PHP 7.4+ with specific extensions; Apache is the primary documented target, with nginx as a sample config
